request.spec:
A plan on a sheet may name one of the sheet's descendants (a sheet id on the plan form; PLAN_ADDED
gains sheet=<id> at its end; a sheet that is not a descendant is refused). Its claims are then
generated for the person of the same name on that sheet (none when there is no such person), by
that sheet's rules and written in that sheet's audit; the plan still counts what it made.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A plan on a sheet may name one of the sheet's descendants (a sheet id on the plan form; PLAN_ADDED
gains sheet=<id> at its end; a sheet that is not a descendant is refused). Its claims are then
generated for the person of the same name on that sheet (none when there is no such person), by
that sheet's rules and written in that sheet's audit; the plan still counts what it made.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A plan can now name one of its sheet's descendants, and its claims are made on that sheet. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec. After that run I only edited a comment in one endpoint file, so I didn't run it again.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V94__plan_sheet.sql`, adds a nullable `target_sheet` column to `plan`. When it's empty, the plan works on its own sheet as before.
- **Adding a plan:** the form has a new optional `plan-form-sheet` field. If a sheet is given and it isn't a descendant of the plan's sheet, the add is refused with `plan-error` and nothing is written. `PLAN_ADDED` gets ` sheet=<id>` at the end only when a sheet was named, so existing plans' audit lines are unchanged.
- **Generating:** in `GeneratePlanClaims.java`, a plan with a target sheet looks up the person with the same name on that sheet. If there is no such person, it makes nothing. Otherwise the claims are added on that sheet using its holidays, terms and periods, and `CLAIM_ADDED` / `LATE_ENTRY` go to that sheet's audit. The plan's made-count includes these claims, and the generate count reports them.
- **Plan row:** shows "on sheet …" (`plan-sheet`) when a plan names a sheet.

**Choices I made that the request didn't cover:**
- **Which "today" applies:** plan dates still run up to the plan's own sheet's today, not the target sheet's. The test needs this: the child sheet's today stays 2026-03-01 but gets claims dated 03-06 and 03-11.
- **"Same name":** I matched it with the existing `findByName`, so an alias on the target sheet also counts.
- **Archived target sheet:** a plan pointing at one is skipped during generate, with no error shown.
- **Validity checked only when added:** if the descendant link is removed later, the plan keeps making claims on that sheet.
